name: RRP

paper.title: Reliable Reasoning Path: Distilling Effective Guidance for LLM Reasoning With Knowledge Graphs

construction.unit: reasoning path: chain of KG triples from a question entity (e0 -r1-> e1 ... -rn-> en)
construction.kept_as: KG triples as given (Freebase); paths generated per question, not stored
construction.processing: no per-question writing; offline, an LLM is fine-tuned on shortest question-answer paths and a GNN path model is trained with bidirectional distribution losses

organization.structure: knowledge graph (Freebase subgraph; Wiki-Movie for MetaQA)

retrieval.query: question; GloVe+LSTM encoding decoded into n reasoning instructions for the GNN
retrieval.candidates: union of LLM-generated semantic paths and GNN structural paths
retrieval.selection: score λ1·cos(LLM question, path) + λ2·cos(GNN question, mean path entity), drop below θ, sort descending
retrieval.budget: threshold θ (best 0.6 on WebQSP); number of paths not stated

use.context: question + surviving paths listed in order of importance
use.reasoning: single answer call (fine-tuned LLaMA2-Chat-7B, or any LLM plug-and-play)

classify.note: A KGQA method, not an agent memory: the store is a fixed knowledge graph that is never written. Candidates come from a fine-tuned LLM and a trained GNN; a fixed weighted score with a threshold (not a reranker model) decides what the answer model reads. How entities in the question are linked to the KG is not stated.

stages.organization: Knowledge lives in an existing KG (a Freebase subgraph for WebQSP/CWQ, Wiki-Movie for MetaQA-3); the method adds nothing to it.
stages.retrieval: A fine-tuned LLM generates semantically relevant reasoning paths, and a GNN that propagates over relation embeddings for n steps generates structurally related paths; each path is scored by a weighted sum of LLM-embedding and GNN-embedding cosine similarity with the question, paths below θ are dropped and the rest sorted.
stages.answer: The question and the kept paths, listed most important first, go to the answer LLM with a prompt asking for all possible answers as a list.
stages.learning: Offline: the path-generating LLM (LLaMA2-Chat-7B) is fine-tuned to maximise the likelihood of shortest question-to-answer paths (KL to a uniform posterior over them); the GNN is trained with KL losses to gold forward/backward entity distributions plus a Jensen-Shannon term tying forward and backward steps.

summary: KG question answering that merges LLM-generated and GNN-mined reasoning paths and keeps only those whose combined semantic and structural similarity to the question passes a threshold, ordered by that score in the answer prompt.
notes:
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering vol. 38 no. 4, pp. 2380-2393, 2026 (DOI 10.1109/TKDE.2026.3656900; PolyU Scholars Hub and IEEE Xplore 11361203). The arXiv v1 PDF is the one read; the TKDE version was not accessible. No official code: the paper links none, the PolyU record lists none, and a GitHub search found only an unrelated third-party 'Modified-Reliable-Reasoning-Path'.
DESIGN: §IV-A to IV-C (Eqs. 1-11, Algorithms 1-2), §V-B (training settings, λ), §V-F (θ), Figs. 5-6 (prompts). Not a memory system in the agent sense: included as KG-based retrieval of reasoning paths. 'rerank' tag = the Rethinking module's score-and-sort step, a fixed formula over learned embeddings. How LLM-generated paths are grounded to KG entities, the number of generated paths, n (hops) and the exact θ used for Table I are not stated.

sources.paper: arXiv 2506.10508v1 (PDF read 2026-09-30); TKDE record checked for venue
sources.code_note: No code: neither the arXiv PDF nor the TKDE record links a repository, and no official repository was found. Everything below comes from the paper's text, equations, Algorithms 1-2 and prompt figures.

headline: The 'memory' is a fixed knowledge graph; RRP decides which reasoning paths through it reach the answer model.
Two generators propose paths (a fine-tuned LLM and a trained GNN); a weighted similarity score with a threshold keeps and orders them.
Paths are handed to the answer LLM most important first, which is the point of the paper's case study.

units.name: Reasoning path
units.role: a chain of KG entities and relations starting at a question entity
units.made_by: fine-tuned LLM (semantic set) or GNN over the KG (structural set)

fields.name: entities and relations
fields.what: e0 → r1 → e1 … → en, taken from the KG

fields.name: semantic score S1
fields.what: cosine between the LLM's embedding of the question and of the path

fields.name: structural score S2
fields.what: cosine between the GNN question vector and the mean of the path's entity vectors

fields.name: source label
fields.what: semantic or structural origin of the path
fields.src: shown in the case study (Table VI); the answer prompt (Fig. 6) does not say it is included

write.how: for each training (question, answer) pair, find the shortest KG paths from question entity to answer entity
LLaMA2-Chat-7B trained to generate those paths from the question (prompt of Fig. 5)

question encoded by GloVe + LSTM and decoded into n instructions; entities initialised from their relations' embeddings; n message-passing steps give entity distributions trained forward and backward (KL + JS)

read.how: GNN propagates over the KG for n steps; paths read off the final entity distribution
drop paths with S ≤ θ, sort the rest by S, highest first

answer_context.sees: the question and the kept reasoning paths
answer_context.format: instruction that paths are listed in order of importance and all possible answers should be returned as a list, then 'Reasoning Paths:' and 'Question:'

compression.basis: Not reported: the paper gives no path counts before or after filtering.

open_questions: Table I compares against baseline numbers whose source (rerun or copied) the paper does not state.
How generated semantic paths are checked against or grounded in the KG is not described, so it is unclear whether they can contain hallucinated relations.
The ablation is on WebQSP only; the CWQ setting (λ2 = 0.9, mostly structural) is not ablated.

abstract.text: RRP targets knowledge-graph question answering, arguing that LLMs need not only facts from a KG but well-ordered reasoning paths through it. It produces candidate paths two ways: a fine-tuned LLM proposes paths that match the question's meaning, and a graph model trained with relation embeddings and forward/backward consistency proposes paths that match its structure. A rethinking step scores every path on both views, discards weak ones and sorts the rest before they are given to the answer model. The authors report state-of-the-art Hits@1 on WebQSP and CWQ with a 7B model, and large gains when the paths are given to other LLMs without fine-tuning.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

components.role: Generate semantic paths; embed question and paths for S1
Generate structural paths; embed for S2
components.model: GNN with GloVe + LSTM question encoder and relation embeddings
fine-tuned LLaMA2-Chat-7B (Table I); GPT-4o-mini, ChatGPT, Alpaca-7B, Flan-T5-xl plug-and-play (Table II)

discussion.takeaway: For KG question answering, which reasoning paths the LLM sees and in what order matters: combining LLM-proposed and graph-mined paths and ranking them lifts a 7B model above prior KG+LLM methods on WebQSP and CWQ.

claims.claim: State of the art among KG-enhanced LLM methods with a 7B model.
claims.evidence: WebQSP Hits@1 90.0 vs RoG 85.7 and SubgraphRAG+LLaMA3-8B 86.6; CWQ 64.5 vs RoG 62.6. Table I, §V-D

claims.claim: The paths help other LLMs without fine-tuning.
claims.evidence: WebQSP Hits@1: GPT-4o-mini 67.08 → 91.10, Flan-T5-xl 30.95 → 69.66; CWQ GPT-4o-mini 41.43 → 71.68. Table II

claims.claim: Semantic and structural paths complement each other, and Rethinking adds on top.
claims.evidence: WebQSP Hits@1 90.0 full, 86.7 without structural, 77.4 without semantic, 88.3 without Rethinking. Table V
MetaQA-3 (Wiki-Movie) 99.5 vs RoG 89.0; inference 2.9 s vs 2.6 s. Tables III-IV

limits: The paper has no limitations section; §V-F notes that a high θ discards valid paths and that the best λ differs by dataset.
reading: This is KG question answering with trained retrievers, not conversational or agent memory: nothing is written or updated per interaction.

Semantic paths with Rethinking reach 86.7, one point above RoG's 85.7; adding the GNN's structural paths gives 90.0. Without semantic paths the score falls to 77.4, so the fine-tuned LLM generator carries most of the performance.
λ is set per dataset (0.5/0.5 on WebQSP, 0.1/0.9 on CWQ); θ and λ1 are chosen from sweeps reported on WebQSP (Figs. 3-4), and the paper does not say whether a validation split was used.
Table I baselines include numbers with ChatGPT and LLaMA2-70B; the paper does not say whether they were rerun or copied, and several cells are blank.
The best result in Table II (GPT-4o-mini + RRP, 91.10 on WebQSP) uses the paths generated by the fine-tuned 7B pipeline with a stronger answer model.
Case study (Table VI) labels each path semantic or structural, but the answer prompt in Fig. 6 does not show whether these labels are given to the model.
